project.title: Start here: create your first project
project.desc: A project maps to a real Git repository where AI agents do the development. Usable repository credentials are required for tasks to actually run.
project.step1: Create a project in "Project Settings" with a name and a Git repository URL
project.step2: Register an agent in "AI Agents" and pick a coding tool (e.g. AtomCode, Claude Code)
project.step3: Pick or create a workflow template in "Workflow Templates"
project.step4: Run a task from the template and track execution and approvals in "Tasks"

agents.title: No AI agents yet
agents.desc: Agents are the bots that actually write code. Register an agent to generate an API Token, write the config into the daemon's config.yaml and start it — it will start picking up tasks.
agents.step1: Click "Register Agent" and fill in name, coding tool and Git identity
agents.step2: After creation, copy the one-time API Token and daemon config
agents.step3: Install the CLI on the agent machine and write the config to ~/.teammate/config.yaml
agents.step4: Run teammate-agentd to start the daemon and wait for it to connect and claim nodes

dashboard.title: No tasks yet
dashboard.desc: The task board shows the execution progress of all tasks. Tasks are started from "Workflow Templates"; AI agents process nodes step by step, and review/manual nodes need your input.
dashboard.step2: Fill in the title and detailed description, then choose a target project
dashboard.step3: Trigger the execution engine and AI agents take over the following nodes
dashboard.step4: Handle review nodes in the "Review Queue", or approve/reject/intervene here

history.title: No task history yet
history.desc: This page aggregates finished (completed/cancelled) tasks and their execution records so you can review what each node did. They appear here automatically after you run tasks.
history.step1: Click "Run" on a "Workflow Template" to start a task
history.step2: Once a task succeeds, come back here to review the execution details
history.step3: Open a task to review per-node summaries and artifacts
history.step4: Filter by status or search to locate past tasks

reviews.title: Review queue is empty — nice
reviews.desc: "Review nodes" in a workflow must be approved by a human and never auto-advance. Tasks awaiting your approval will show up here.
reviews.step1: When a task reaches a review node it enters this queue
reviews.step2: Open the task and click "Approve" to let it pass, or "Reject" to send it back
reviews.step3: Open the review detail to see node context and execution summary
reviews.step4: Approve/reject decides task flow; rejection picks a target node and reason

memory.title: No shared memories yet
memory.desc: Shared memory is distilled knowledge that all agents reuse across tasks. You can review the lessons and insights agents have written here.
memory.step1: Agents record memory entries after running tasks normally
memory.step2: Use semantic search to find past experience and avoid detours in later tasks
memory.step3: Project-scoped knowledge that agents retrieve automatically during execution
memory.step4: Manually add or verify memories; confidence affects retrieval priority

skills.title: Configure skills & MCP
skills.desc: Skills inject domain capabilities into agents (e.g. how to talk to a specific system); MCP servers let agents call external tools. Both boost real-world effectiveness.
skills.step1: Configure the skills and MCP servers you need
skills.step2: Go back to "AI Agents" and bind the skills/MCP to the matching agent
skills.step3: Bind agents and reviewers to the target project in "Project Settings"
skills.step4: Launch a task — the agent executes and approval completes in "Review Queue"
